string.text: Independent Chernobyl State
Independence is our salvation
NChG flag: the Chernobyl plant and a radiation sign
NChG emblem: the state motto and its landmark, the Chernobyl plant

We, the people of the Chernobyl exclusion zone, united by a common fate and history, proclaim the creation of the Independent Chernobyl State for the sake of freedom, safety and the preservation of our land.
Chapter I. Foundations of the System
Article 1. The NChG is a sovereign military state.
Article 2. The state religion and ideology are survival and defence of the territory.
Article 3. The territory of the NChG is inviolable. Any violation of the borders is equated with military aggression.
Article 4. Symbols of the NChG: the flag (the plant and a radiation sign) and the emblem (the motto and the landmark, the plant).
Chapter II. Citizens
Article 1. A citizen of the NChG is anyone who formally renounced the citizenship of other countries and has lived in the zone for at least one year.
Article 2. The basic rights of a citizen: the right to life, the right to protection, the right to work, the right to take part in politics.
Article 3. The basic duties of a citizen: service in the army or state bodies, observance of the Constitution and the laws, and defence of the NChG territory against external and internal threats.
Chapter III. The President and Power
Article 1. The President of the NChG is the head of state and of the armed forces.
Article 2. The President is elected for five years but may be removed early by the People's Council.
Article 3. The President must: command the army, sign laws, appoint ministers, and oversee state security.
Chapter IV. Organs of Power
Article 1. The People's Council is the body representing every organisation (gang) of the zone.
Article 2. The Prosecutor's Office and the Courts of the NChG are the organs of justice.
Article 3. The Chernobyl Guard Service (ChSO) is an elite body ensuring the safety of the President and of the state.
Chapter V. Economy
Article 1. The economy of the NChG rests on production (factories, plants) and trade (shops, stalls, pharmacies).
Article 2. The currency of the NChG is the Chernobyl Rouble (ChR).
Article 3. The state has the right to set controlled prices on essential goods.
Chapter VI. Security
Article 1. The armed forces of the NChG are the guarantor of independence.
Article 2. Every citizen is obliged to undergo military training.
Article 3. The state has the right to apply the death penalty to traitors, betrayers and spies.
Chapter VII. Final Provisions
Article 1. Amendments to the Constitution may be introduced only by the People's Council or by the President.
Article 2. The Constitution enters into force immediately upon its adoption.
Chapter VIII. Jurisprudence

Article 1. The jurisprudence of the NChG is a system of bodies and officials ensuring fairness, protection of rights, observance of the laws and maintenance of public order. All holders of legal office act in the interests of the NChG, subject to the Constitution and the general laws.
Article 2. The main offices in jurisprudence are: prosecutor, investigator, judge, defence lawyer, legal counsel and notary.
Article 3. The duties of holders of legal office are set out in this chapter and in the Constitution of the NChG.
Prosecutor
Supervision of law enforcement and initiation of cases.
Investigator
Conducting investigations, gathering evidence, identifying the guilty.
Judge
Hearing cases and passing decisions.
Defence lawyer
Defending the accused and representing the interests of citizens.
Legal counsel
Legal advice and assistance in concluding contracts.
